agent_notes: An angel's call is the effect of Abraham's raised knife; the link is explicit in 22:10–12.

The oath (22:16) is expressly 'because you have done this thing'. Its fulfilment is in later chapters (22:17 offspring like the stars, 22:18 nations blessed); the Gen 24–26 sessions should write the FULFILLS_PROPHECY links, for example 26:3–5 where God repeats the oath to Isaac.

22:6–8 form one continuous ascent with the dialogue; the two 'they went both of them together' (22:6, 22:8) bracket it. The duration of 2 hours is an estimate and gives no hour of the day; DAY_SEQUENCE because it falls within the day of the sighting.

'On the third day' counted inclusively: day 1 is the departure day, so the sighting is START of departure + 2 days, margin 12 hours. Rashi explains the delay as keeping Abraham from acting in a daze. Whether the Hebrew day (sunset to sunset) shifts this count is not answered; the margin covers it.

The text does not say how long after the command he rose. 'Early in the morning' is taken as the first morning after the command, so offset 0 and BOKER. Pseudo-Jonathan names Eliezer and Ishmael as the two servants; I follow the Hebrew.

Journey time: `urim travel loc.beersheba loc.moriah_mount --mode donkey` gives 70 km straight, c. 88 km by road, 4 km/h, 21.9 h moving, elapsed about 2 days. This agrees with the text's third day (the first day counted as day one). Ibn Ezra says he left from Beersheba; Radak reads the third day as the day he reached Jerusalem's border and saw the place.

The text says only 'after these things'. Isaac's age is not given: Targum Pseudo-Jonathan has him 36–37, and the other chapters' anchors (Isaac born c. 2066 BCE, Gen 21 events c. 2064 BCE) leave a gap. Following the reviewer request, I anchored on the START of Isaac's birth with offset 25 years and margin 12 years (Isaac c. 13–37), bounded below by Ishmael's departure and above by Sarah's death in Gen 23 (Isaac 37). The centre is a guess; Pseudo-Jonathan's 36 lies near the upper end.

Divine speeches: 22:1–2 (command, followed by 22:3 obedience; a TRIGGERS link, not FULFILLS_PROPHECY), 22:8 (Abraham's word, fulfilled at 22:13), 22:11–12 and 22:15–18 (angel's words; the promise of 22:17–18 has no fulfilment in this chapter). The place 'which I will tell you' (22:2) is reached at 22:9 and I wrote no prophecy link for it since the text shows no separate telling.

agent_notes: 'After these things' with no figure. Rashi has Abraham told on his return from Moriah, and Pseudo-Jonathan on the road; I put the news at the end of the return with a margin of a year because the births themselves are undated. Rebekah's birth is reported as a fact before this point; it dates only by the Gen 24–25 chain (Isaac 40 at marriage), so no anchor is set from it.
